edges.notes: Eligible motor route: a rotary joint assembly may use a frameless torque motor when selected for the design; the edge does not require that motor in every assembly.

Eligible alternative transmission route: a rotary joint assembly may use a harmonic reducer; selection among harmonic, RV, and precision planetary reducers is architecture-dependent, not a simultaneous BOM requirement.

Eligible alternative transmission route: a rotary joint assembly may use an RV reducer; selection among harmonic, RV, and precision planetary reducers is architecture-dependent, not a simultaneous BOM requirement.

Eligible alternative transmission route: a rotary joint assembly may use a precision planetary reducer; selection among harmonic, RV, and precision planetary reducers is architecture-dependent, not a simultaneous BOM requirement.

Eligible feedback route: a rotary joint assembly may integrate a joint encoder module when required by its sensing architecture; the edge does not require simultaneous use of every eligible component.
Eligible safety route: a rotary joint assembly may integrate a joint brake where holding or emergency restraint is required; the edge does not make a brake universal.

Eligible support route: a rotary joint assembly may use a shared joint-bearing design selected for its load and packaging requirements; the edge does not prescribe one universal bearing configuration.
Eligible alternative linear-drive route: a linear joint assembly may use a planetary roller screw; screw and direct-drive alternatives are architecture-dependent, not simultaneous BOM requirements.
Eligible alternative linear-drive route: a linear joint assembly may use a ball screw; screw and direct-drive alternatives are architecture-dependent, not simultaneous BOM requirements.
Eligible alternative linear-drive route: a linear joint assembly may use a trapezoidal screw; screw and direct-drive alternatives are architecture-dependent, not simultaneous BOM requirements.

Eligible alternative linear-drive route: a linear joint assembly may use a direct-drive linear motor instead of a screw transmission; alternatives are architecture-dependent, not simultaneous BOM requirements.
Eligible support route: a screw-driven linear joint assembly may use a screw support bearing selected for its load and speed requirements; direct-drive routes may not require it.
Eligible feedback route: a linear joint assembly may use a linear displacement sensor when direct extension feedback is required; the edge does not make it universal.
Eligible upper-limb actuation route: a shoulder module may integrate shared rotary joint assemblies selected for its degrees of freedom and load requirements.
Eligible upper-limb actuation route: an elbow module may integrate a shared rotary joint assembly selected for its kinematic and load requirements.
Eligible upper-limb actuation route: a wrist module may integrate shared rotary joint assemblies selected for compact multi-axis motion.
Eligible lower-limb actuation route: a hip module may use rotary joint assemblies; rotary and linear routes are architecture-dependent and this edge does not fix the design.
Eligible lower-limb actuation route: a hip module may use linear joint assemblies; rotary and linear routes are architecture-dependent and this edge does not fix the design.
Eligible lower-limb actuation route: a knee module may use a rotary joint assembly; rotary and linear routes are architecture-dependent and this edge does not fix the design.
Eligible lower-limb actuation route: a knee module may use a linear joint assembly; rotary and linear routes are architecture-dependent and this edge does not fix the design.
Eligible lower-limb actuation route: an ankle module may use rotary joint assemblies; rotary and linear routes are architecture-dependent and this edge does not fix the design.
Eligible lower-limb actuation route: an ankle module may use linear joint assemblies; rotary and linear routes are architecture-dependent and this edge does not fix the design.
Eligible hand-actuation route: a dexterous hand assembly may use finger micro-actuators when compact distributed actuation is selected; the edge does not make the route universal.
Eligible hand-transmission route: a dexterous hand assembly may use micro-reducer transmissions where local torque multiplication is selected; the edge does not require every hand to use them.

Eligible alternative hand-transmission route: a dexterous hand assembly may use tendon or flexible transmission when remote actuation is selected; the edge does not require simultaneous use with micro-reducers.
Eligible sensing-control route: a dexterous hand assembly may integrate fingertip tactile-force control when the manipulation requirements justify it; the edge does not make it universal.

Eligible cross-chain dependency: a humanoid robot battery pack may select cells owned by the primary canonical battery_high_specific_energy_cell node; robot requirements do not transfer generic cell ownership.

Eligible cross-chain dependency: a humanoid robot battery pack may integrate a platform owned by the primary canonical battery_management_system_platform node; robot requirements do not transfer generic BMS ownership.

Cross-chain dependency: model training and inference platforms require accelerator modules; accelerator-module ownership remains with ai_compute_infrastructure, while chip ownership remains with ai_logic_compute_chips.
Cross-chain dependency: large-model training and serving may require rack-scale AI systems; F1 owns the model service layer rather than servers or racks.
Cross-chain dependency: training corpora, checkpoints, and serving artifacts require distributed AI storage owned by ai_compute_infrastructure.
Cross-chain dependency: distributed model workloads use high-speed cluster switching without transferring networking ownership to F1.
Cross-chain dependency: model jobs use cluster scheduling software owned by ai_compute_infrastructure; F1 owns model lifecycle and serving behavior.
Cross-chain dependency: fine-tuning, evaluation, vector retrieval, and RAG workflows use distributed storage while storage ownership remains external.
Cross-chain dependency: model adaptation workflows may submit jobs through the canonical compute cluster scheduler; the toolchain does not own compute orchestration infrastructure.

Cross-chain dependency: aircraft electric propulsion may require high-specific-energy cells; generic battery ownership remains with power_batteries_battery_materials and does not create a direct F2 company mapping.
Cross-chain dependency: aircraft energy systems may use a BMS platform; generic BMS ownership remains with power_batteries_battery_materials.
Cross-chain dependency: aircraft inverters may use SiC power devices; device ownership remains with power_semiconductors and generic chip revenue does not qualify for F2.

Eligible NTN research route only: a 6G air-interface candidate may use satellite-specific ground access and terminal integration for laboratory or field validation. Satellite ownership remains with satellite_communications_navigation_remote_sensing, and this edge does not imply 6G commercial deployment or revenue.

Eligible manufacturing dependency: mature-node foundry flows may depend on KrF lithography equipment. Equipment ownership remains with semiconductor_manufacturing_equipment; G2 ownership is limited to the wafer-manufacturing platform. Canonical ownership does not transfer（所有权不转移）.

Analog and BCD foundry processes use foundry-specific PDK and design-enablement flows. EDA, IP and PDK ownership remains with semiconductor_eda_ip_design_services; G2 does not own chip design. Canonical ownership does not transfer（所有权不转移）.

G1 MEMS-specific process research may depend on the cross-product manufacturing platform represented in G2. MEMS device and MEMS-specific research ownership remains with mems_intelligent_sensors; the edge does not duplicate company ownership. Canonical ownership does not transfer（所有权不转移）.

Power MOSFET devices depend on an eligible high-voltage wafer-manufacturing process. Device product and company ownership remains with power_semiconductors; G2 owns only the evidenced manufacturing-process platform. Device ownership does not transfer（器件所有权不转移）.

A silicon-carbide power device depends on an eligible compound-semiconductor wafer-manufacturing process. SiC device product and company ownership remains with power_semiconductors; G2 owns only the manufacturing platform and keeps an evidence gap until direct foundry proof exists. Device ownership does not transfer（器件所有权不转移）.

Civil aero-engine blades, disks, rings and hot-section casings use high-end metal-cutting and grinding equipment. Machine-tool ownership remains with industrial_machine_tools_cnc; this dependency does not transfer company or revenue ownership（所有权不转移）.

Civil-aircraft composite structures may use multi-axis composite machining centers. Machine-tool ownership remains with industrial_machine_tools_cnc; the edge does not transfer generic material, equipment, company or revenue ownership（所有权不转移）.

Commercial-fission reactor pressure vessels, steam generators and directly evidenced nuclear pressure-boundary equipment use large metal-cutting and grinding machine tools. Machine-tool ownership remains with industrial_machine_tools_cnc; equipment, company and revenue ownership does not transfer（所有权不转移）.

Nuclear-qualified forgings, castings, pipes and components use high-end metal-cutting and grinding equipment. Nuclear component ownership remains with nuclear_power_equipment and machine-tool ownership remains with industrial_machine_tools_cnc（所有权不转移）.
